faq.q: Which contexts does it preview my thumbnail in?
faq.a: Six YouTube contexts rendered at real pixel sizes: desktop search (360x202), mobile search (320x180), home feed grid (246x138), suggested/sidebar (168x94), watch-page end screen, and channel page. Plus six other platforms: Instagram feed, Instagram 1:1 grid crop, Facebook link preview, Twitter/X card, LinkedIn post, and WhatsApp forward. You can toggle YouTube dark and light modes.

faq.q: What does the Legibility Checker report?
faq.a: It shows your image's dimensions and aspect ratio (flagging anything that isn't ~16:9), warns if the image is below 1280x720, and estimates the smallest original text size likely to stay readable at the 168px sidebar render. It also samples the image to report average brightness and contrast range out of 255, with suggestions if the thumbnail is too dark, too bright, or low-contrast.

faq.q: Can I compare two thumbnail designs?
faq.a: Yes. Upload Thumbnail A and Thumbnail B in the A/B Comparison section and they're rendered side by side in the four key YouTube contexts (desktop search, mobile search, home grid, sidebar) as a table, so you can judge which design reads better at each size before publishing.

faq.q: How can I export or share the previews?
faq.a: Three ways: 'Export Contact Sheet PNG' draws all contexts into one labelled image; 'Download all previews (ZIP)' bundles one PNG per platform using JSZip; and 'Copy preview' copies a single selected platform's render to your clipboard as a PNG (where the browser supports ClipboardItem). Overlays simulate the duration badge, red progress bar, and title text, and safe-area guides mark the regions those cover.
